provenance.note: Owner-authorized chapter 4 production authoring, 5 October 2026. Structural order, canonical/source identities, known response counts, recorded support, occurrence targets and dependencies retain unified S29/S32 evidence. Japanese wording, readings, translations, banks, mappings, contextual examples and static kanji teaching are reviewed authoring/adaptation from retained targets, not source quotations. Both full Japanese-only game dialogues are authored replacements; no observed turn count is claimed. Comprehension/replay references bind to the appropriate earlier scene. A02 S08 is a separate transcript-free losing-state clip. 負 uses reviewed kun まける/おう and on ふ with word-specific voiced ぶ in 勝負; source notation is not copied as a universal reading. Four-response verb conversion and five-character compound reconstruction preserve physical counts. Typed go tasks explicitly accept 行け/いけ; romanized ike is instructional reading evidence only. Two selected imperatives grade as one exact-set screen with no partial credit. Only the two documented misses receive a single retry at the end of their first internal activity. No production endpoint or speaking action is introduced.

policies.assessment: Equal weight per graded screen; exact-set multi-selection has no partial credit. Core completion, immutable first-attempt accuracy, separate retry mastery and checkpoint pass reporting remain distinct.
policies.incorrectResponses: Final choices/token placement and explicit Check lock feedback; wrong pairs permit correction but retain first-attempt mistakes. Only configured wrong occurrences retry once after their activity. Completing the retry, even incorrectly, permits continuation.
policies.audio: Existing Japanese TTS replaces unavailable audio/video. Required playback and ordered all-turn dialogue gates apply. Transcript-free clips hide source and translation until feedback; scene replay exists only where configured.
policies.visuals: Original media and animations are deferred. Complete static glyph shape/readings/examples and replaceable media slots retain teaching. No invented stroke-order or etymology claims.

unresolvedSourceFacts: Source-identical literal wording, exhaustive accepted variants, randomization, acoustic alignment and original media remain unavailable; authorized authoring supplies complete production copy.
Source rewards, scoring formula, exactly-80 pass boundary and causal unlock enforcement remain unresolved. No research results seed learner progress.
Source recap drawer contents and universal retry behavior were not observed; explicit scene replay and occurrence-only boundary policies are app configurations.

screens.prompt: Complete the positive and negative evaluation points.

after.text: この計画の良い点と悪い点を考えます。
after.secondary: このけいかくのよいてんとわるいてんをかんがえます。

after.text: I will consider this plan’s good and bad points.
良い点（よいてん）and 悪い点（わるいてん）are positive and negative aspects. 点 describes an evaluation point here; 店 would describe a shop.

audio.text: この計画の良い点と悪い点を考えます。
audio.reading: このけいかくのよいてんとわるいてんをかんがえます。
audio.feedbackText: この計画の良い点と悪い点を考えます。

screens.prompt: Type the imperative of 行く in Japanese, then select Check.

after.text: 行け！
after.secondary: いけ！

after.text: Go!

This occurrence accepts 行け and いけ explicitly. Romanized ike may explain the reading but is not accepted by this Japanese-script task. No automatic kana/romaji conversion applies. The imperative is a strong direct command. It occurs in urgent instructions and sports cheering, but can sound rude in ordinary requests. Use てください for a polite request. Relationship and context matter; cheering does not make commands universally polite.

audio.text: 行け！
audio.reading: いけ！
audio.feedbackText: 行け！

after.secondary: いまはれいたいいちでまけています。

screens.prompt: Build the five-chunk negative sports intention.

after.text: 週末は、サッカーをしないつもりです。
after.secondary: しゅうまつは、さっかーをしないつもりです。

after.text: I intend not to play football this weekend.
Negative plain verb + つもりです expresses an intention not to act: 負けないつもりです. 負ける is a RU/ichidan verb: remove る and add ない. This intention is not a guarantee of the eventual result.

audio.text: 週末は、サッカーをしないつもりです。
audio.reading: しゅうまつは、さっかーをしないつもりです。
audio.feedbackText: 週末は、サッカーをしないつもりです。

screens.prompt: Type the intention expression after 勝つ. です is supplied.

after.text: 次の試合に勝つつもりです。
after.secondary: つぎのしあいにかつつもりです。

after.text: I intend to win the next match.

Dictionary-form verb + つもりです states an intention: 勝つつもりです. Keep the verb plain before つもり, even when the final copula is polite. This builds on earlier verb classes and intention expressions; it is not a claim of first introduction.

audio.text: 次の試合に勝つつもりです。
audio.reading: つぎのしあいにかつつもりです。
audio.feedbackText: 次の試合に勝つつもりです。

screens.prompt: Complete the past intention and actual result.

after.text: 勝つつもりでしたが、負けました。
after.secondary: かつつもりでしたが、まけました。

after.text: I intended to win, but lost.
Verb + つもりでした describes a past intention, which may differ from the actual result. 勝つつもりでしたが、負けました means I intended to win, but lost. Future 勝つつもりです differs from past 負けました.

audio.text: 勝つつもりでしたが、負けました。
audio.reading: かつつもりでしたが、まけました。
audio.feedbackText: 勝つつもりでしたが、負けました。

screens.prompt: Reconstruct five characters in the sports, rank and victory compounds.

after.secondary: やきゅうのたいかいでいちいになり、ゆうしょうしました。

野球 is やきゅう; 一位 is いちい; 優勝 is ゆうしょう. These are five character placements, not five sentence chunks.

screens.prompt: Complete the past near-miss adjective in two parts.

after.text: 昨日の試合は、惜しかったです。
after.secondary: きのうのしあいは、おしかったです。

after.text: Yesterday’s match was a near miss.
惜しい（おしい）reacts to a near miss or something almost achieved. Its past is 惜しかった: remove final い and add かった. 残念（ざんねん）expresses broader regret or disappointment, and need not imply a close miss.

audio.text: 昨日の試合は、惜しかったです。
audio.reading: きのうのしあいは、おしかったです。
audio.feedbackText: 昨日の試合は、惜しかったです。

screens.prompt: Choose the imperative of する in the coach’s command.

after.text: 毎日、練習しろ！
after.secondary: まいにち、れんしゅうしろ！

after.text: Practise every day!
練習する → 練習しろ. する is dictionary form; して is te form. せよ is another imperative used in more formal/written contexts, but is not a choice in this task.

惜しい（おしい）reacts to a near miss or something almost achieved. Its past is 惜しかった: remove final い and add かった. 残念（ざんねん）expresses broader regret or disappointment, and need not imply a close miss.

screens.prompt: Complete the past disappointment and continued support.

after.text: 昨日は残念でしたが、これからも応援します。
after.secondary: きのうはざんねんでしたが、これからもおうえんします。

after.text: Yesterday was disappointing, but I will keep supporting them.
残念でした places the disappointment in the past. これからも応援します states continuing support from now on, despite that result.

audio.reading: きのうはざんねんでしたが、これからもおうえんします。

screens.prompt: Complete the disappointment word and past copula for sold-out tickets.
scaffold: チケットが売り切れていて、

after.text: チケットが売り切れていて、残念でした。
after.secondary: ちけっとがうりきれていて、ざんねんでした。

after.text: The tickets were sold out, which was disappointing.
残念 is a na-adjective/noun: 残念です → 残念でした. It expresses disappointment about a result or unavailable opportunity. It differs from the close-miss focus of 惜しい, though both can fit some real situations.
